n030300a1168.s: A lasting fall in the general price level is called:
n030300a1168.x: Deflation is a fall in the price level (negative inflation); disinflation is only a fall in the inflation rate, which stays positive.

n6b02637ceb5.s: Inflation running below 3% a year is called:
n6b02637ceb5.x: Creeping inflation is below 3%; walking inflation is about 3-10%, and galloping inflation precedes hyperinflation.

nindian-economy-51-3.s: Headline inflation is more volatile than core inflation mainly because headline inflation includes:
nindian-economy-51-3.x: Headline inflation includes food and energy prices, which swing sharply; core inflation leaves them out and is more stable.

n322070bfcf9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the uses of price indices?
o: CPI is used for revising dearness allowance
The GDP deflator is used for industrial workers' dearness allowance
WPI is used for contract escalation
WPI is used for industrial analysis
n322070bfcf9.x: Industrial workers' dearness allowance uses CPI-IW, not the GDP deflator; CPI is used for DA and WPI for contract escalation and industrial analysis.

n2c0cd1b79fe.s: Which of the following pairs about inflation in May 2026 is correctly matched?
o: Consecutive months AP stayed above the national rate – three
n2c0cd1b79fe.x: AP's retail inflation was 4.9% against India's 3.9% in May 2026, and AP stayed above the national rate for five consecutive months.

nindian-economy-44-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the shifting of tax burden?
o: The burden of GST is generally shifted through prices
Property tax is a direct tax
The burden of property tax can be shifted through prices
nindian-economy-44-2.x: Property tax is a direct tax and its burden cannot be shifted through prices; GST, an indirect tax, is passed on through prices.

ne38d175b692.s: During the early planning decades, India's tax revenue was dominated by:
o: Direct taxes such as income and corporation tax
Indirect taxes such as excise, customs and sales tax
ne38d175b692.x: Excise, customs and sales taxes (indirect taxes) dominated in the early planning decades; direct taxes dominate now.

nf7e0dbab221.s: MODVAT was introduced in India on:
nf7e0dbab221.x: MODVAT came on 1 March 1986; CENVAT followed on 1 April 2000, Haryana's VAT on 1 April 2003 and nationwide State VAT on 1 April 2005.

n1d4f895d069.s: The Laffer curve, with zero tax revenue at both a 0% and a 100% tax rate, has the shape of:
n1d4f895d069.x: Revenue is zero at the two extreme rates and positive in between, so the Laffer curve is an inverted U.

ncada171aad7.s: Under the new tax regime, a salaried individual pays no income tax on income up to:
ncada171aad7.x: The ₹12 lakh Section 87A rebate limit plus the ₹75,000 standard deduction gives the ₹12.75 lakh threshold for salaried individuals.

n1643b41e51e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MAT under Budget 2026-27?
o: It was made a final tax
New MAT credit continues to be allowed after 1 April 2026
Before the change, MAT was 15% of book profits
n1643b41e51e.x: Budget 2026-27 cut MAT from 15% to 14% and made it a final tax; no new MAT credit is allowed after 1 April 2026.

nabd4504247d.s: Securities transaction tax (STT) was introduced in India in:
nabd4504247d.x: STT came in 2004; estate duty was 1953, wealth tax 1957 and gift tax 1958.

n5472b8d965b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT)?
o: It was abolished with effect from 1 April 2020
Dividends are now taxed only in the hands of the company paying them
Dividends are now taxed in the hands of shareholders
n5472b8d965b.x: After DDT was abolished from 1 April 2020 by Budget 2020-21, dividends became taxable in the shareholders' hands, not the company's.

new.s: A fall in the inflation rate from 3% to 2% is an example of:
new.x: Disinflation is a fall in the rate of inflation that stays positive; prices still rise, only more slowly.

new.s: Walking (trotting) inflation refers to an annual rate of about:
new.x: Walking inflation is about 3-10% a year; creeping inflation is below 3%.

new.s: Food inflation in India is measured by the Consumer Food Price Index, which has how many sub-groups?
new.x: The CFPI has 10 sub-groups, including cereals, pulses, vegetables, milk and spices.

new.s: Which measure reflects the underlying long-run trend of inflation, ignoring short-term swings?
new.x: Core inflation excludes volatile food and fuel, so it shows the underlying trend and is more stable.

new.s: Inflation caused by a sharp fall in supply while demand stays the same, from structural shortages, is called:
new.x: Bottleneck inflation arises from structural supply shortages (farm productivity, storage, distribution) and is hard for government to tackle.

new.s: Inflation caused by strong export demand draining domestic supply is called:
new.x: Export-led inflation occurs when strong export demand drains domestic supply.

new.s: Which of the following does NOT cause demand-pull inflation?
new.x: Demand-pull comes from expansionary policy, fiscal stimulus and public spending; rising interest rates do not cause it.

new.s: A rise in wages, raw material costs and fuel prices leads to which type of inflation?
new.x: Cost-push inflation results from rising input costs such as wages, raw materials, fuel and a falling rupee.

new.s: The dominant cause of inflation in India is:
new.x: Supply shocks – erratic monsoon, El Nino, costlier crude and rupee depreciation – are the dominant cause of inflation in India.

new.s: The Brent crude oil benchmark comes from which region?
new.x: Brent is the North Sea benchmark; WTI and Dubai are the other two main benchmarks.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about inflation in India:
1. MSP hikes and hoarding add to inflation.
2. Inflation expectations can feed inflation.
3. Better storage and distribution efficiency worsens supply shocks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: MSP hikes, hoarding and expectations add to inflation; better storage and distribution ease supply shocks, so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about factors behind stagflation in India:
1. Inflation from higher government spending
2. A fall in industrial production and slow growth
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Stagflation combines inflation (e.g. from higher government spending) with falling industrial production and slow growth.

new.s: The cost to firms of repeatedly re-pricing goods during inflation is called:
new.x: Menu costs are the costs of repeated re-pricing during inflation.

new.s: Which group is hurt most by inflation?
new.x: Creditors are hurt most because they are repaid in money of lower real value; debtors gain.

new.s: During deflation, the purchasing power of money:
new.x: When prices fall, each unit of money buys more, so purchasing power rises.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the effects of inflation?
new.x: Fixed-income groups are exposed unless their incomes are adjusted; they are not automatically protected.

new.s: CPI-AL and CPI-RL are compiled on which current base year?
new.x: Since June 2025 the Labour Bureau's CPI-AL and CPI-RL use base 2019 (earlier 1986-87).

new.s: The linking factor of CPI-AL for Andhra Pradesh is:
new.x: The CPI-AL linking factor is 10.72 for AP, against 9.69 for India (CPI-RL 9.78).

new.s: The Labour Bureau, which compiles CPI-IW, is headquartered at:
new.x: The Labour Bureau, set up in 1920 under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is at Chandigarh.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a Labour Bureau index?
new.x: CPI-UNME (Urban Non-Manual Employees) is the odd one out; CPI-IW, CPI-AL and CPI-RL are Labour Bureau series.

new.s: What is the weight of food and beverages in the new CPI (base 2024)?
new.x: Food and beverages carry 36.75% in the new CPI; the 2012 series had about 46%.

new.s: The new CPI series (base 2024) has how many divisions under COICOP 2018?
new.x: The new CPI has 12 divisions under COICOP 2018, against 6 groups earlier.

new.s: The new WPI series on base 2022-23 contains how many items?
new.x: The new WPI (base 2022-23) has 957 items; the 2011-12 series had 697.

new.s: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) measures:
new.x: IIP measures industrial output, not prices; it is released by NSO.

new.s: Which index measures prices at the first-point bulk (wholesale) stage?
new.x: WPI measures wholesale, first-point bulk prices; CPI measures retail prices.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the weights in price indices:
1. Food has a bigger weight in CPI than in WPI.
2. Manufactured goods carry the biggest weight in WPI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Food carries more weight in CPI than in WPI, while manufactured goods (64.23%) carry the biggest weight in WPI.

new.s: On whose committee's framework did the RBI adopt CPI (Combined) as the headline measure in April 2014?
new.x: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) made CPI the nominal anchor under flexible inflation targeting.

new.s: The working group on WPI revision to base 2011-12 was headed by:
new.x: Saumitra Chaudhuri's group (set up March 2012) gave the 2011-12 base; Abhijit Sen's gave 2004-05.

new.s: Who headed the working group for the WPI base 2022-23?
new.x: Ramesh Chand of NITI Aayog led the working group for the 2022-23 WPI base (2025).

new.s: Under the RBI Act, which Section provides for a six-member Monetary Policy Committee?
new.x: Section 45ZB sets up the six-member MPC; 45ZA covers target-setting and 45ZN the breach report.

new.s: Section 45ZN of the RBI Act was first invoked in:
new.x: Section 45ZN, requiring a report after three consecutive quarters of band breach, was first invoked in 2022.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about flexible inflation targeting in India?
o: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement was signed in February 2015
new.x: The target is 4% with a 2-6% band; 6% is only the upper limit, not the target.

new.s: In the original Phillips curve, lower unemployment comes with:
new.x: Phillips (1958) found an inverse relation: lower unemployment goes with higher (wage) inflation.

new.s: About what share of India's workers are informal, weakening wage bargaining and flattening the Phillips curve?
new.x: About 92% of workers are informal, so wage bargaining is weak and India's Phillips curve is fairly flat.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's inflation in 2025:
1. CPI inflation was 2.2%, a 12-year low.
2. Food inflation was -0.2%, the first food deflation since 2014.
3. Food inflation was higher than headline inflation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: In 2025 CPI was 2.2% and food -0.2%, so food was below headline (order Core > Headline > Food).

new.s: India's CPI inflation in August 2026 was 4.8%, described as a:
new.x: August 2026 CPI inflation of 4.8% was a 20-month high.

new.s: What was the order of food, headline and core inflation in the year 2025?
new.x: In 2025 food inflation was negative (-0.2%), so the order was Core > Headline > Food, unlike 2023-24 and May 2026.

new.s: Under OMSS (Domestic), the FCI sells:
new.x: OMSS (Domestic) is the FCI's sale of wheat and rice; pulses and onions belong to the Price Stabilisation Fund buffer.

new.s: The Price Stabilisation Fund maintains a buffer of:
new.x: The PSF holds a buffer of pulses and onions; wheat and rice are sold under OMSS by the FCI.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of anti-inflation tool and its type is correctly matched?
new.x: OMO sale of securities is monetary; buffer-stock release is supply-side; taxes and spending are fiscal.

new.s: Bharat Chana Dal, sold from July 2023, was priced at:
new.x: Bharat Chana Dal was sold from July 2023 at ₹60/kg through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar.

new.s: India's onion export ban was lifted on 4 May 2024 with an export duty of:
new.x: The ban was lifted on 4 May 2024 with a 40% duty and US$550 MEP; the duty was cut to 20% on 13 September 2024.

new.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the DES monitors the prices of how many essential commodities daily?
new.x: AP's DES monitors 8 essential commodities daily; groundnut and palm oil were added in February 2025.

new.s: For the government, inflation-indexed bonds mainly offer:
o: Protection of investors' nominal return only
Higher interest costs during low inflation
Cheaper borrowing when credible on inflation
new.x: For government, IIBs give cheaper borrowing when it is credible on inflation and signal commitment to low inflation.

new.s: For investors, inflation-indexed bonds mainly provide:
o: A fixed nominal coupon unaffected by prices
new.x: IIBs link principal and/or interest to an inflation index, protecting the investor's real return.

new.s: A levy described as a 'tax on tax' for a specific purpose, ending once the purpose is met, is a:
new.x: A cess is levied for a specific purpose and ends when the purpose is met; it is not shared with States.

new.s: The Clean Energy Cess on coal (2010) was renamed in Budget 2016-17 as the:
new.x: The Clean Energy Cess on coal, from the Finance Act 2010, was renamed Clean Environment Cess in Budget 2016-17.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT levied by States or local bodies?
new.x: Customs duty is a Union levy; profession, entertainment, road and property taxes are levied by States or local bodies.

new.s: How many taxing entries does the State List contain?
new.x: The Union List has 15 taxing entries, the State List 20 and the Concurrent List 3.

new.s: Residuary taxing power, under which gift, wealth and expenditure taxes were levied, rests with:
new.x: Residuary taxing power lies with Parliament, the basis of gift, wealth and expenditure taxes.

new.s: Under Article 276, the annual ceiling on profession tax is:
new.x: Article 276 caps the State profession tax at ₹2,500 a year.

new.s: Securities transaction tax (STT), collected by the stock exchange, is classified as a:
new.x: STT is a direct tax though collected by the exchange; it came from 1 October 2004.

new.s: The person who finally bears the burden of a tax is said to bear its:
new.x: Impact is on whom the tax is first imposed; incidence is who finally bears it.

new.s: Direct taxes in India are administered by the CBDT, while indirect taxes are administered by the:
new.x: Direct taxes are administered by the CBDT and indirect taxes by the CBIC.

new.s: Wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty are called 'paper taxes' because they:
o: Were levied only on paper industries
new.x: These direct taxes never yielded much revenue, hence the name 'paper taxes'.

new.s: Under GST, the taxable event is the:
new.x: GST is levied on supply; excise was on manufacture, VAT on sale and customs on import or export.

new.s: The taxable event for service tax was the:
new.x: Service tax was levied on the provision of a service; it is now subsumed in GST.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of tax and taxable event is correctly matched?
new.x: Customs is levied on import or export; excise is on manufacture, VAT on sale and GST on supply.

new.s: A tax charged at one rate for all income levels is called:
new.x: A proportional tax has one rate for all; a flat-rate sales tax is an example.

new.s: India's tax system is best described as:
o: Progressive in nature but overall degressive
new.x: Progressive direct taxes combine with regressive indirect taxes, making the system progressive in nature but overall degressive.

new.s: A tax under which the poor pay a higher share of their income than the rich is called:
new.x: Under a regressive tax the poor pay a higher share of income; GST on essentials and excise are examples.

new.s: What is the share of direct taxes in gross tax revenue in the 2026-27 Budget Estimate?
new.x: Direct taxes are 61.2% of gross tax revenue in 2026-27 BE, against 38.8% for indirect taxes.

new.s: According to the Economic Survey 2009-10, the share of excise in gross tax revenue fell from 30.4% in 2005-06 to:
new.x: Excise share fell sharply from 30.4% (2005-06) to 20.8% (2007-08).

new.s: In the 2026-27 BE, direct taxes are about what percentage of GDP?
new.x: Direct taxes are 6.9% of GDP and indirect taxes 4.3% in 2026-27 BE.

new.s: In the Centre's rupee for Budget 2026-27, the largest single item of receipts overall is:
new.x: Borrowings and other liabilities are 24%, the largest overall; income tax at 21% is the largest tax.

new.s: Which is the largest component of the revenue receipts of the States?
new.x: Own tax revenue is about half of States' revenue receipts (FY25); share in central taxes is second.

new.s: SGST accounts for about what share of Andhra Pradesh's own-tax revenue in 2024-25 (RE)?
new.x: SGST, ₹36,296 crore, is about 38% of AP's own-tax revenue; State Excise is about 22%.

new.s: India's average tax-GDP ratio for 2001-22 was about:
new.x: India averaged 16.36% in 2001-22, the lowest among emerging economies and below the OECD.

new.s: The combined (Centre and States) tax-GDP ratio of India is about:
new.x: The combined ratio is about 19.6%; the Centre's is about 11.5% post-pandemic and States' own tax about 7% of GSDP.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the tax-GDP ratio:
1. A low ratio points to a large informal sector or high tax evasion.
2. A falling ratio means revenue is growing slower than GDP.
3. The World Bank regards 25% as the tipping point.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: A low ratio reflects informality or evasion and a falling ratio means buoyancy below 1; the World Bank tipping point is 15%, not 25%.

new.s: Tax buoyancy, unlike tax elasticity, includes the effect of:
o: Discretionary changes in tax rates and base
new.x: Buoyancy includes discretionary changes in rates and base; elasticity excludes them.

new.s: In the 2026-27 BE, the buoyancy of direct taxes is:
new.x: Direct tax buoyancy is 1.1 against 0.3 for indirect taxes and 0.8 gross.

new.s: The Laffer curve is associated with which economist (1974)?
new.x: Arthur Laffer drew the curve in 1974; the term was coined by Jude Wanniski.

new.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, buoyant revenues helped bring the fiscal deficit in FY26 down to:
new.x: Buoyant revenues helped the fiscal deficit fall to 4.4% of GDP in FY26.

new.s: The Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee that proposed VAT in India was set up in:
new.x: The L.K. Jha Committee (1976) proposed VAT at the manufacturing stage, leading to MODVAT.

new.s: The first State to adopt VAT in India was:
new.x: Haryana adopted VAT on 1 April 2003; State VAT became nationwide on 1 April 2005.

new.s: The Parthasarathi Shome committee of 2012 dealt with:
new.x: Shome (2012) reviewed GAAR and recommended dropping retrospective tax; the 2013 TARC on administration was also under him.

new.s: Budget 2015-16 raised the service tax rate from 12% to:
new.x: Service tax rose from 10% to 12% in 2006-07 and from 12% to 14% in Budget 2015-16.

new.s: Service tax was introduced in India, on the advice of the Chelliah Committee, in:
new.x: Service tax came in 1994-95 on Chelliah's advice.

new.s: India's first income tax of 1860 was introduced by James Wilson, who was the:
o: First Finance Minister of independent India
new.x: James Wilson, the first Finance Member, introduced income tax in 1860 (Act assent 24 July 1860).

new.s: The 1997-98 'dream budget' cut income-tax rates to:
new.x: FM P. Chidambaram's 1997-98 budget cut rates to 10, 20 and 30% from 15, 30 and 40%.

new.s: Under the new tax regime slabs from Budget 2025-26, income of ₹4-8 lakh is taxed at:
new.x: Income up to ₹4 lakh is nil and ₹4-8 lakh is taxed at 5%.

new.s: The standard deduction available to salaried taxpayers under the new regime is:
new.x: A ₹75,000 standard deduction takes the salaried tax-free limit from ₹12 lakh to ₹12.75 lakh.

new.s: What change did Budget 2026-27 make to the new-regime income-tax slabs?
o: Raised the rebate limit to ₹15 lakh
new.x: The Budget 2025-26 slabs remain unchanged in 2026-27.

new.s: The approximate effective tax rate for existing domestic companies under Section 115BAA is:
new.x: Section 115BAA has a 22% base rate and an effective rate of about 25.17%.

new.s: The approximate effective tax rate for new manufacturing companies under Section 115BAB is:
new.x: Section 115BAB has a 15% base rate and an effective rate of about 17.01%.

new.s: After being withdrawn in 1990, MAT was restarted in the Budget of:
new.x: MAT came in Budget 1987-88, was withdrawn in 1990 and restarted in Budget 1996-97.

new.s: Angel tax, levied from 2012 on share premium of unlisted start-ups, was abolished in Budget:
new.x: Angel tax was abolished in Budget 2024-25.

new.s: The Cost Inflation Index used for indexation of capital gains has the base year:
new.x: The CII, notified by CBDT, has base year 2001-02.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about special direct taxes:
1. Estate duty was introduced in 1953 and abolished in 1985.
2. Wealth tax was introduced in 1957 and abolished in 2015.
3. Gift tax is still in force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Estate duty ran 1953-1985 and wealth tax 1957-2015; gift tax was abolished in October 1998.

new.s: Gift tax, introduced in April 1958, was abolished in:
new.x: Gift tax was abolished in October 1998.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about capital gains?
o: Capital gains arise on transfer of a capital asset
Rural agricultural land is a capital asset
Tax on sale of inherited property is capital gains tax
Indexation uses the Cost Inflation Index
new.x: Rural agricultural land is not a capital asset; the other statements are correct.

new.s: The Wanchoo Committee (1971) dealt mainly with:
new.x: The Wanchoo (Direct Taxes Enquiry) Committee of 1971 dealt with black money and evasion.

new.s: The Committee on taxation of agricultural wealth and income (1972) was headed by:
new.x: K.N. Raj's committee (1972) dealt with agricultural wealth and income; it was not Chelliah.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of committee and focus is correctly matched?
o: Justice R.V. Easwar – Simplifying the Income-tax Act
new.x: Easwar (2015-16) worked on simplifying the Income-tax Act; Rustagi on CBDT restructuring, Akhilesh Ranjan on the DTC and Wanchoo on black money.

new.s: Nicholas Kaldor's 1956 report recommended which taxes?
o: Expenditure, wealth, gift and capital gains taxes
new.x: Kaldor (1956) recommended expenditure, wealth, gift and capital gains taxes.

new.s: The Income Declaration Scheme 2016 carried a total levy of:
new.x: IDS 2016 carried 45%; PMGKY 50% and FAST-DS 60%.

new.s: The Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act was passed in:
new.x: The Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act was passed in 2020; a second scheme came in 2024.

new.s: Under FAST-DS 2026, the general disclosure limit for foreign assets of small taxpayers is:
new.x: The limit is ₹1 crore, or ₹5 crore for previously taxed but unreported assets.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about black money disclosure schemes:
1. The Income Declaration Scheme ran from 1 June to 30 September 2016.
2. PMGKY 2016 carried a lower levy than IDS 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: IDS ran from 1 June to 30 September 2016 at 45%; PMGKY carried a higher 50% levy.

new.s: Which Act withdrew retrospective tax demands in cases such as Vodafone and Cairn?
new.x: The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 withdrew retrospective demands; the Finance Act 2012 had imposed them.

new.s: The equalisation levy of 6% introduced in 2016 applied to:
new.x: The 6% levy (2016) was on online ads and was abolished from 1 April 2025; the 2% levy (2020) was on e-commerce.

new.s: The OECD/G20 BEPS project has how many actions against profit shifting?
new.x: BEPS has 15 actions against MNC profit shifting to low-tax places.

new.s: The Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force with effect from:
new.x: The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act with effect from 1 April 2026, not 2025.

new.s: The Income-tax Act, 1961 came into effect on:
new.x: The 1961 Act took effect from 1 April 1962.

new.s: The task force whose 2019 report dealt with the Direct Taxes Code was headed by:
new.x: The Akhilesh Ranjan task force reported on the Direct Taxes Code in 2019.

new.s: The CBDT is a statutory body under the:
new.x: CBDT is statutory under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963, and sits in the Department of Revenue.

new.s: Faceless appeals in income tax were launched in:
new.x: Faceless assessment came on 13 August 2020 and faceless appeals in September 2020.

new.s: Budget 2026-27 cut TCS on LRS remittances for education and medical purposes from 5% to:
new.x: TCS on LRS for education and medical was cut from 5% to 2% in 2026-27.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about tax administration?
o: e-Sahyog is an online compliance check of mismatches
CBDT is in the Department of Expenditure
new.x: CBDT is in the Department of Revenue, not Expenditure; the other statements are correct.
